title: Her Wedding
description:
The Han family's wedding was on another scale.

A five-star hotel grand ballroom. The ye-dan alone — the formal betrothal gifts the two families exchange — ran to tens of millions of won. The guest list traded names from business and politics. His future father-in-law said,
"It's my daughter's wedding. It has to be done without embarrassment. You understand that much, don't you?"

{name} understood that 'that much' exceeded his entire net worth.

And the seating — the bride's side would fill with names everyone knew.
On the groom's list, {name}... could barely write a few. His father, Hyunsu, and blank space.

choices.text: "I'll make it work." Go into debt to stand at that level.
choices.result_text:
He took on debt to match the ye-dan, and filled the empty groom's seats with employees from Jiyeon's company.

A wedding without embarrassment. On the surface.

After the ceremony, {name} looked at his side again. Most were faces he didn't know.
He'd stood at the level of her world. On the very tips of his toes.

choices.text: "I can't do that. I want to do it within my means."
choices.result_text:
His father-in-law's face hardened. Jiyeon looked at {name} without a word.

"...It's fine. I've got you, oppa. That's all I need," Jiyeon said.
But at the end of those words, something flickered, just for a moment. Disappointment, or resignation.

{name} stood as himself. Only — the distance between her world and his became visible for the first time that day.

description_if_known.told_jiyeon_about_records:

A five-star hotel grand ballroom. The ye-dan alone ran to tens of millions of won. The guest list traded names from business and politics. His future father-in-law said,
"It's my daughter's wedding. It has to be done without embarrassment."

{name} knows where all of it — the ballroom, the ye-dan, those names — came from. Han PD Construction. The name at the bottom of a list, over a decade ago, that ruined his father.
And Jiyeon knows it now too.

They stand facing each other in a hall paid for with that money, both of them knowing. The groom's seats were still bare. {name} looked back and forth between those empty chairs and the bride's side across from them.

title: The Kind of Man He'd Be
description:
Five years are ending. Gangnam stayed out of reach.

For the first time in a while, Jiyeon sat him down, serious.
"I'll be honest, oppa. I never figured you for the kind of guy who'd live like this."

"I wasn't asking for anything huge. But you... somewhere along the way you just stopped. Dodging anything risky, settling for something small."

"I can't tell if that's stability or just giving up. My father calls it giving up."

Her eyes waited for an answer. Whatever {name} said now, this marriage hung on it.

choices.text: "I'll change. I'll fit your world. Anything." (Hold on to her)
choices.result_text:
From that day {name} decided to become someone else. He went into her father's business, learned the rules of that world, did things he never used to.

Jiyeon stayed. The marriage held.

But years later, looking in the mirror — the man standing there wasn't the one who ate triangle kimbap five years ago.
He kept her. Only, the man he kept her with was no longer himself.

choices.text: "This is me. I can't change it. ...I'm sorry." (Let her go)
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon looked at him for a long time. She didn't get angry. She wasn't the type.

"...I know. You're a good person, oppa. You're just not from my world."

She went back to her world. To a life that suited it, with someone who suited it.

{name} never reached Gangnam, and lost her too. But the face in the mirror was still his.
Small and whole, and traded for nothing.

description_if_known.namsan_lock_jiyeon:
Five years are ending. Gangnam stayed out of reach.

Jiyeon sat across from him, serious for once.
"I'll be honest. I didn't know you were someone who'd live like this."

Namsan came to mind. The night she called it childish and took a photo anyway, and hung the lock.
That lock would still be there. Whatever became of us.

Her eyes waited for an answer. On whatever {name} said now, this marriage hung.
